Subject: Zephyr security questionnaire — residency & retention section

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for taking this. Attached is the small section of our security questionnaire focused on data residency, retention windows, backups, and deletion procedures. We need concise answers we can pass to our InfoSec team — ideally bullet points or short paragraphs for each question.

Key asks:
- Where is hosted API customer content stored by default (region)?
- How long are request logs/inputs/outputs retained?
- Process & SLA for a customer-initiated deletion request
- What happens to backups/snapshots and cached KV material?

We appreciate anything you can share. Please attach any short matrix or artifact we can add to our vendor risk assessment.

Thanks,
Daniel
Daniel Huang
Security Engineer | ZephyrCorp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Zephyr security questionnaire — residency & retention section

Hi Daniel — thanks for the questionnaire. Below are succinct answers you can paste into the Zephyr vendor assessment. I attached a one-page CSV matrix (residency_matrix_2025.csv) that maps data types to storage region and retention bands for hosted API customers.

1) Default storage location / data residency
- Hosted API default: data is stored in the region you select at the account level (us-west, us-east, eu-west). If no selection, resources default to us-west.
- We operate regionally isolated object and block stores per-region; customer request payloads and generated outputs for that account are written to the chosen region.
- Metadata used for routing and metrics (non-content telemetry) may be replicated for operational telemetry but does not contain user prompt/response content.

2) Retention windows (hosted API) — default behavior
- Request payloads and generated outputs (customer content): retained for 30 days by default to support debugging and quality monitoring; can be configured by enterprise customers (down to 0 days) via Contract Addendum.
- Request logs (request id, timestamps, error codes): retained 90 days. Logs include no plaintext model outputs unless enabled by customer for advanced debugging.
- Aggregated telemetry & metrics: retained for 24 months (anonymized and aggregated).

3) Deletion / erasure process and SLA
- Deletion channels: 1) Self-serve deletion request form (admins) 2) Support ticket with deletion tag 3) Contractual Data Erasure statement for legal/regulated requests.
- Active store removal: within 14 calendar days after a validated request we remove customer content from active storage and mark related indices for purge.
- Backup & snapshot deletion: snapshots are removed on a 90-day window; we attempt to purge blobs referencing the content within 90 days.
- Forensic & audit logs: immutable audit trails required for compliance are retained up to contractually agreed windows (default 12 months) unless otherwise specified in order/contract.
- Confirmation: we provide a deletion attestation (signed PDF) when the erasure workflow completes.

4) Backups, snapshots, and KV cache behavior
- Short-lived KV caches (model state / inference cache) are in-memory or ephemeral and flushed on instance termination; these are not persisted to durable backups.
- Persistent backups / nightly snapshots: customer content may be captured in encrypted snapshots. We maintain a snapshot lifecycle where snapshots older than 90 days are expired and garbage-collected.
- When a deletion request is processed we mark matching objects and schedule background reclamation across snapshot indices; final physical removal from backups can take up to 90 days.

5) Encryption & key management
- Data at rest: AES-256 encryption using customer-segregated keys for enterprise customers or Redwood-managed KMS for standard hosted plans.
- In-transit: TLS 1.2+ for all endpoints.
- Enterprise option: HSM-backed keys and customer-managed KMS integration (bring-your-own-key).

6) Human access & review
- By default there is no human review of customer prompts/outputs. Access to content for debugging or safety review requires explicit customer opt-in & an audited access workflow (ticket + 2 approvers).

Process notes / next steps
- If Zephyr needs shorter default retention we can propose a Contract Addendum (e.g., 0/7/30-day profiles).
- To initiate a verified deletion request please use: https://drive.google.com/open?id=redwood-deletion-request-form (link below) — include account ID and requested scope.

I hope this helps — Kimberly (security) and Aditya (infra) are copied if you need deeper technical examples or attestation language for your assessment.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — very helpful. Quick follow-up on backups & KV caches so we can close this section with InfoSec:

- You mention KV caches are ephemeral / in-memory. Can you confirm whether any portion of the inference KV cache is ever written to local disk on the serving nodes (e.g., for warm-start/rebuild)? If yes, are those disks encrypted and included in the snapshot lifecycle?
- For the snapshot reclamation: do you provide an API or ticket-based attestation that specifically lists the objects removed (e.g., object ids or snapshot ids) or just a signed statement that the deletion workflow completed?

If you can provide one or two sentences we can paste, that's ideal.

—Daniel

Hi Daniel — quick clarifications from security/infra:

- KV cache persistence: Redwood inference runtime keeps the KV cache in RAM; we do not persist raw KV cache contents to local disk as part of normal operation. In rare proactive warm-start scenarios we may write encrypted checkpoint artifacts to local encrypted disks to accelerate rebuilds; such artifacts are short-lived and included in the same snapshot lifecycle and GC schedule. All local disks are encrypted (LUKS / cloud-provider disk encryption) and part of the 90-day snapshot reclamation window.

- Deletion attestation: we provide a signed deletion attestation PDF for standard deletion requests (includes account ID, scope, and timestamp). For enterprise customers under tighter contractual terms we can also provide a list of object ids / snapshot ids removed (redacted as needed) via an encrypted report delivered through the secure portal.

If you want formal language for your vendor RFI, you can use: "Redwood retains customer content in the selected region and will remove content from active stores within 14 days of a validated erasure request. Backup snapshots containing the content are scheduled for garbage collection and physical reclamation within 90 days; Redwood will provide a signed attestation upon completion. Short-lived inference caches are held in memory; any temporary checkpoint artifacts written to encrypted local disks are included in the snapshot reclamation process."

Happy to jump on a quick call if your InfoSec team wants to review.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
